elements.justification: st.turn_lane: 'a lane designated only for turning; side ∈ {left, right}', with side right: the 'right lane to be used only for turning'. The rule reads that lane where the subject is in it, through rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'). 'Designed to provide' is read as the lane's presence on the road (observable_reading, category status). 'Single' adds no restriction: every st.turn_lane is a lane used only for turning, so the duty for a vehicle in a right turn lane is the same whether or not a second right turn lane runs beside it (residue, scope none).

'Vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', with the definition's exclusions recorded by the reading under that id); ru.aggregate is 'true when the user carries an included class'. It is never expanded.

'Be driven in the right turn lane': the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) the region t of kind st.turn_lane, side right, that s1 selects; 'the right turn lane' singles out that same lane, so the obligation binds t again with the whole selection of s1 (kind turn_lane, side right, occupied by the subject) and judges every such lane. 'Driven' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading, category agency). The s4 intention is read at this same lane t: the purpose the words attach is the purpose of being in that lane, so the intention's target region is t, anchored to the subject by rel.occupies.

intentions.meaning: the source's current plan for the road user includes leaving the target lane by a turn to the right made at the lane's end, the plan's preparation for that turn included

residues.why: 'single' adds no restriction: every st.turn_lane is a lane designated only for turning, and the duty of a vehicle driven in a right turn lane is the same whether that lane is the only right turn lane or one of several

applicability: The subject, a vehicle, occupies (rel.occupies) some region t of kind st.turn_lane whose side is right.
obligation: At every observation, for every region t of kind st.turn_lane with side right that the subject occupies (the whole selection of s1 restated), the subject's declared intention int.right_turn_from_lane holds at t, read at the judged observation: its plan leaves that lane by a right turn at the lane's end, whether the turn is made into an intersection, a driveway or an alley entrance. Where it is declared false at such a lane the duty is violated; where it is undeclared there (the pair absent or the id left out) and no such lane makes it violated, it is unknown.

narrowings.why: 'designed to provide' is read through the right turn lane's presence on the road
'driven' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject occupies a st.turn_lane of side right that enters an intersection, and int.right_turn_from_lane is declared false for the subject at that lane (its plan goes straight through the intersection).

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The subject occupies the right turn lane and int.right_turn_from_lane is declared true for the subject at that lane (its plan turns right at the intersection the lane enters).

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject occupies a through st.lane beside the right turn lane; no turn lane is occupied.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The source labels lanes but cannot tell a turn lane; the subject occupies the rightmost lane, labelled lane, with int.right_turn_from_lane declared false at it.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject occupies a st.turn_lane of side left with int.right_turn_from_lane declared false at it: no right turn lane is occupied.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The subject occupies a right turn lane whose end meets a driveway entrance and enters no intersection, and int.right_turn_from_lane is declared true at that lane (its plan turns right into the driveway).
